page_title: Notes apps are where ideas go to die. And that’s good.

summary.title: Notes apps are where ideas go to die. And that's good.
summary.one_liner: Notes and bookmarking tools work mainly by making us feel safe forgetting, so the act of writing things down matters more than the app or retrieval.
keywords: why do i save notes i never reread
takeaways: We write things down partly to forget them, and the sense of safety that a notes app provides is what lets us let go.
Loss aversion makes us hoard ideas and bookmarks we rarely need, which can overload our attention.
Most saved notes have little value on their own; the valuable few tend to resurface on their own.
The act of writing an idea down is what helps imprint it, more than the app or its organization features.
A plain scratchpad or document can serve the same purpose as a sophisticated notes app.
summary.summary: This essay argues that people write things down, bookmark, and save links mainly to forget them, feeling safe that the material can be retrieved later. It draws on David Allen's GTD, Daniel Kahneman's work on loss aversion, and writers such as William Germano, Stephen King, and Dan Shipper, whose experience with Roam Research is cited. The author notes that people keep switching apps (Evernote to OneNote, Roam to Obsidian) hoping for a better system, when the real value lies in the writing and the feeling of safe forgetting. The piece is an opinion essay with no tutorial steps.
